verses.text: In those days Israel had no king. A Levite who lived in a remote area of the hill country of Ephraim took a concubine, a second wife, from Bethlehem in Judah.
But she was unfaithful to him. She left him and went back to her father's house in Bethlehem in Judah. After she had been there four months,

her husband went to her to speak kindly to her and persuade her to come back. He took his servant and two donkeys with him. She took him into her father's house, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.
His father-in-law, the young woman's father, persuaded him to stay, so he stayed with him three days, eating and drinking and sleeping there.
On the fourth day they got up early, and he got ready to leave. But the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Have something to eat first to give you strength. Then you can go."
So the two of them sat down to eat and drink together. Afterward the woman's father said, "Please stay tonight and enjoy yourself."
When the man got up to go, his father-in-law urged him to stay, so he stayed there that night too.
On the morning of the fifth day he got up early to leave, but the woman's father said, "Have something to eat to give you strength. Wait until afternoon!" So the two of them ate together.

Then the man, with his concubine and his servant, got up to leave. But his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said, "Look, it is almost evening. Please spend the night here. The day is nearly over. Stay and enjoy yourself. Early tomorrow morning you can get up and go home."
But the man did not want to stay another night. He got up and left, and went toward Jebus, which is Jerusalem, with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.
When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone, the servant said to his master, "Come, let us stop at this city of the Jebusites and spend the night."
His master replied, "No. We will not go into a city of foreigners, where the people are not Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah."
He added, "Come, let us try to reach Gibeah or Ramah and spend the night in one of those places."
So they went on, and the sun set as they came near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
They stopped there to spend the night in Gibeah. They went and sat in the city square, but no one took them into their home for the night.
That evening an old man came in from his work in the fields. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was living in Gibeah. The people of the place were from the tribe of Benjamin.
When he looked and saw the traveller in the city square, the old man asked, "Where are you going? Where did you come from?"

He answered, "We are on our way from Bethlehem in Judah to a remote area in the hill country of Ephraim, where I live. I have been to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the LORD. No one has taken me into their house.
We have straw and food for our donkeys, and bread and wine for ourselves, for me, your servant woman, and the young man with us. We do not need anything."
"You are welcome at my house," the old man said. "Let me take care of whatever you need. Only do not spend the night in the square."
So he took him into his house and fed his donkeys. After they had washed their feet, they had something to eat and drink.

While they were enjoying themselves, some wicked men of the city surrounded the house. They pounded on the door and shouted to the old man who owned the house, "Bring out the man who came to your house so we can have sex with him."
The owner of the house went outside and said to them, "No, my friends, do not be so evil. This man is my guest. Do not do this terrible thing.
Look, here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out to you now. You can abuse them and do whatever you want to them. But do not do such a terrible thing to this man."
But the men would not listen to him. So the Levite took his concubine and sent her outside to them. They raped her and abused her all night, and at dawn they let her go.
At daybreak the woman went back to the house where her master was staying. She fell down at the door and lay there until it was light.
When her master got up in the morning and opened the door of the house to go on his way, there lay his concubine, fallen in the doorway, with her hands on the doorstep.
He said to her, "Get up. Let us go." But there was no answer. Then he put her on his donkey and set out for home.
When he reached home, he took a knife and cut her body into twelve parts, limb by limb, and sent them into all the areas of Israel.
Everyone who saw it was saying to one another, "Such a thing has never been seen or done, not since the day the Israelites came up out of Egypt. Just imagine! We must do something! So speak up!"
